newsitem.title: UK: Shell dip on Q3 earnings but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Shell dip on Q3 earnings but off lows.

text.p: Shares in Shell Transport and Trading Co, the British arm of Anglo-Dutch oil group Royal Dutch Shell, dropped on Thursday after the group released third quarter earnings figures.

Shell stock, which had stood around 1,021p before the news, dropped as low as 1,013p before recouping some losses to trade three pence lower at 1,017-1/2p some 10 minutes after the announcement. The broader market was slightly weaker.
Shell said current cost net income excluding special items in the third quarter totalled 1.117 billion stg after 1.202 billion a year earlier.
Including special items, current cost net income rose to 1.201 billion stg from 1.117 billion and net income increased to 1.329 billion from 1.053 billion.
Irene Himona, oils analyst at SG Strauss Turnbull, said the income figure excluding items was slightly below forecasts.

"The range was 1.15 billion stg to 1.28 billion. The trends were pretty much as expected and chemicals were much weaker year on year obviously...Overall, there were no great surprises. It's just slightly disappointing," she said.
Himona noted that the return on capital had edged up, while net debt had "practically vanished".
Himona said Shell still had further room for rationalisation and cost-cutting.
She said SocGen had an "undervalued" recommendation on Shell stock and would not change the recommendation as a result of the third-quarter figures.
